transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-07-01 14:00 UTC | Duration: 58m
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lia (Redwood SE), Maya (HalcyonQuant), Derek (CTO), Priya (DevOps), Omar (PM)

Summary note: medium-quality auto transcript, some words mangled.

00:00 Samir: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro from our side, I'm Samir, AE at Redwood, with Lia on the technical side. how's everybody doing?
00:06 Maya: good thanks, little short on time so we'll try to be efficient.
00:10 Samir: perfect. high level, we wanted to map your workload and budget constraints so we can propose the right hosting mix — hosted api, dedicated reserved pools, or private vpc/on-prem.
00:22 Derek: sure. quick context: HalcyonQuant runs inference for pricing signals, mostly short-context prompts ~80-300 tokens output, a mix of classification and light generation for feed enrichment. latency matters but not ultra-low - aiming for 150ms p50, 300ms p95. Budget is tight, we have to keep monthly inference spend under a hard cap for pilot.
00:40 Lia: ok that's helpful — shortish sequences change the math, batching and kv/prefix caching often move the needle a lot there. do you have an idea of qps and burst patterns?
00:48 Maya: baseline ~30 qps, nightly batch peaks at 250 qps for re-scoring jobs, and occasional spikes during market open — short bursts that last minutes.
00:59 Lia: so two workload profiles: steady interactive and bursty batch. that means mixing routing policies could help — route latency-sensitive requests to a lower-batch, lower-utilization pool, and re-score traffic to cheap, high-throughput slots.
01:12 Derek: what's the per-token break between hosted and dedicated roughly? we've seen vendor quotes that are all over.
01:18 Samir: quick rule of thumb — for this profile, hosted api with Redwood's shared capacity tends to be simplest but unit price will be higher because it includes multi-tenant overhead and elastic capacity. Dedicated reserved pools reduce per-token compute by ~20-45% depending on utilization, quantization, and batching. private (VPC) is similar to dedicated in unit compute but we add a small infra surcharge for the private control plane and egress/residency constraints. important caveat: these are model- and sequence-length dependent.
01:44 Maya: can you give numbers? ballpark per 1k tokens?
01:47 Lia: we avoided raw numbers on this call but offered example bands — hosted might be X to Y cents per 1k tokens for a medium-sized model; dedicated can push to about 60-80% of that with heavy batching and kv cache. we'll send a tailored spreadsheet.
02:05 Priya: are there levers we can change from our side to lower cost without sacrificing p95?
02:10 Lia: yes — three high-impact levers: 1) batching windows — increasing aggregation for low-priority requests dramatically improves GPU utilization; 2) KV/prefix cache — for repeated prompt prefixes, the cached KV reduces self-attention compute; 3) quantization/ model variant — switching to int8 or a trimmed architecture for certain routes. Each has latency tradeoffs.
02:31 Derek: how bad is the latency hit for batching? we can't let some flows exceed our SLO.
02:36 Lia: there's a spectrum — micro-batches (20-50ms windows) give big uplift in throughput with minimal p95 change. larger windows (100-200ms) cut cost further but start to affect p95. you can also multi-tier: latency-critical calls routed to a low-latency lane (no batching) and background scoring to a high-batch lane.
02:53 Maya: we heard about KV cache — our prompts often reuse a 40-token system prompt, then vary the rest. is that a big win?
03:01 Lia: yes. prefix/KV caching frequently reduces per-call compute by 30-60% for short variable tails because you only compute the new tokens rather than reprocessing the whole prefix. best case when you have long shared context. we'll show simulated savings in the spreadsheet.
03:16 Omar: any gotchas for us if we go private VPC? network complexity, latency to vendor, keys?
03:22 Samir: with Redwood Private you get a control plane that can be customer-managed in your VPC. KMS integration is supported (customer KMS/HSM). typical challenges: VPC peering setup, egress rules, and metrics ingestion back to Redwood console if you want cloud-hosted observability. Priya, does that match your expectations?
03:39 Priya: yes, we'll need to check our KMS provider (HashiCorp Vault today) and SAML IdP.
03:44 Lia: we support SAML/SSO and RBAC. audit logs and traceability are available — SOC2 paperwork we'll share. private setups have a longer lead time (2-6 weeks) vs hosted which is immediate.
03:58 Derek: timeline question — from pilot to production, what's realistic?
04:03 Samir: pilot can be 2-4 weeks for hosted or dedicated with reserved pools. private sometimes adds 4-8 weeks depending on networking and compliance gating. success criteria should be defined: cost per 1k tokens, p95 latency, and availability during bursts.
04:18 Maya: on pricing, are there commit discounts for reserved capacity?
04:21 Samir: yes — Dedicated offers monthly/annual reserved capacity with commit discounts. We also support burst capacity add-ons if you want predictable baseline plus burst.
04:31 Omar: security/compliance: do you publish pen test reports?
04:34 Lia: yes, we can share SOC2 type II, pen test summary, and our data retention policies. for legal, we'll need an NDA and then we can push full compliance docs.
04:45 Derek: any performance differences between quantized models running on dedicated vs hosted?
04:49 Lia: quantization benefits are orthogonal to hosting — the serving runtime picks optimized kernels and quantized pathways based on hardware. Dedicated gives you the ability to pin quantized variants with predictable throughput. Hosted might run multiple variants but we provide performance profiles and you can request particular variants for your pilot.
05:03 Maya: for our use — short outputs, repeated prefix — sounds like KV cache + dedicated pool could be big. we just need to see numbers to sell it internally.
05:11 Samir: absolutely. next step we'll run a small benchmark with your sample prompts to show p50/p95 and token-cost deltas across hosted/dedicated/private configs. Lia will own config and we'll provide a cost model.
05:22 Priya: what about data residency? we need EU-only for some datasets.
05:25 Lia: we have region controls and can deploy dedicated/private in EU regions. for hosted if the model runs in EU region it's fine, but if you need customer-managed keys and no egress we recommend Private.
05:36 Derek: any mention of competitors? we evaluated Anthropic and Bedrock but found variable latency and opaque unit costs.
05:43 Samir: yep, those are common. we try to be transparent with per-route token-level analytics so you can map levers to dollars.
05:52 Maya: ok let's recap — send pilot pricing + cost model, share SOC2 and KMS docs, set up benchmark next week. may require NDA.
05:59 Samir: great. thank you all, we'll follow up via email and Slack.
